descripcion_geo: Mesopotamian city mentioned along with Hamat and Arfad in the Assyrian arguments before Hezekiah; Their gods could not resist Assyria.
importancia_estrategica: City used as an argument for Assyrian omnipotence.

historias.titulo: The gods of Ivvá could not resist
historias.descripcion: The Assyrian messenger argues that the gods of Hamath, Arfad, and Ivva did not free their cities from Assyrian power.

historias.titulo: The challenge to Hezekiah with the example of Ivva
historias.descripcion: Sennacherib sends a letter citing Ivva among the peoples whose gods failed: how would Judah expect to be different?

historias.titulo: Hezekiah takes the letter to the Temple
historias.descripcion: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's letter (which mentions Ivvah) before the Lord in the Temple and prays.

personajes.descripcion: He used Ivvá's argument to demoralize the defenders of Jerusalem.
He took Sennacherib's challenge (with mention of Ivvah) to the Temple in prayer.
He answered Hezekiah's prayer: the Lord will protect Jerusalem even though the gods of Ivvah and others fell.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Ivvá: relevant geographical region in the Old Testament.

judaismo.descripcion: Ivva and other cities are used as 'proof' that no god can resist Assyria; God responds by destroying the Assyrian army in one night (2 Kings 19:35).
judaismo.significado_teologico: Ivva and other cities are used as 'proof' that no god can resist Assyria; God responds by destroying the Assyrian army in one night (2 Kings 19:35).
